title: Intelligent control
summary:
Intelligent control is a class of control techniques that use various artificial intelligence computing approaches like neural networks, Bayesian probability, fuzzy logic, machine learning, reinforcement learning, evolutionary computation, and genetic algorithms.

Neural networks have been used to solve problems in almost all spheres of science and technology. A feedforward network with nonlinear, continuous, and differentiable activation functions has universal approximation capability. Bayesian probability has produced algorithms in common use in advanced control systems, such as the Kalman filter and the Particle filter. Fuzzy logic handles uncertainty and imprecision by mimicking human reasoning. Genetic algorithms are optimization techniques inspired by natural evolution used to optimize control strategies.

Intelligent control systems seek to emulate important characteristics of human intelligence, including adaptation and learning, planning under great uncertainty, and coping with large amounts of data. These systems integrate AI techniques with conventional control theory to manage systems that are too complex or uncertain for traditional control methods, designed to learn, adapt, and improve their performance over time.

Applications include robotics, aerospace, automotive systems, industrial automation, and renewable energy. In autonomous vehicles, intelligent control enables real-time decision-making, path planning, and obstacle avoidance. In smart buildings, it orchestrates energy management and climate control. The term intelligent control was formally used for the first time in 1967 by C.T. Leondes, and in 1985 IEEE held the first Symposium on Intelligent Control.
